# Drydock
[mono][color=#897236]BERTHS [/color] 2,500 to 80,000 by hull class[/mono]
[mono][color=#897236]SELL-BACK [/color] half an empty berth's price[/mono]
[mono][color=#897236]OFFERS [/color] 30 minutes to accept or decline[/mono]
[mono][color=#897236]ROUND END [/color] 50% of appraisal to reclaim[/mono]
The Drydock tab on the shipyard console is where your ships wait between shifts. A stored ship sits in a [color=#a4885c][bold]berth[/bold][/color], and retrieving it empties that berth until the ship comes back.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#ffdd33][bold]BERTHS[/bold][/color] ──────────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
Every ship you buy includes a berth of its hull class, created with the purchase. A berth's class comes from the hull's size:
[mono]Cutter up to 96 tiles 2,500\nCorvette up to 192 tiles 5,000\nFrigate up to 384 tiles 10,000\nCruiser up to 768 tiles 20,000\nCapital up to 1,536 tiles 40,000\nSupercapital above 1,536 tiles 80,000[/mono]
- Selling an empty berth refunds half its price. - A hull that outgrows its berth can be upgraded on the spot from the tab, paying the difference between classes. - You may have one civilian ship underway at a time. Buying another ship, or retrieving one, refuses while it is out.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=lime][bold]STORING[/bold][/color] ─────────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
- Dock at the station the console you are using is on. A ship is stored from its berth, not from open space. - Everyone disembarks first, and the ship must carry no armed nuke, no running countdown and no singularity. - Pick a berth from [color=lime]Store in #N[/color]. It names the berth the console would choose and lists every free berth, the ones too small greyed with the reason.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#00ccff][bold]RETRIEVING[/bold][/color] ──────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
- The ship arrives already docked at the station. - A fresh deed lands on the card in the console. - A pending rename, if you queued one, is applied to the hull and the deed together.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#ffa500][bold]WHAT STAYS BEHIND[/bold][/color] ───────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
- Research resets on retrieve. - Contraband found aboard is seized. - Permits come back only for the character who does the retrieving.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#1e90ff][bold]THE SHIP MENU[/bold][/color] ───────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
Each berthed ship has a menu of its own.
- [color=#a4885c][bold]Rename…[/bold][/color] takes effect on the ship's next retrieve. - [color=#a4885c][bold]Move…[/bold][/color] shifts it to another of your berths. - [color=#a4885c][bold]Transfer…[/bold][/color] offers the ship to an online captain with a berth that fits. It waits in escrow for up to 30 minutes while they accept or decline, and they are warned if accepting takes their last free berth. - [color=#a4885c][bold]Sell…[/bold][/color] pays a share of the ship's appraisal and frees the berth. Type the ship's name to confirm; it cannot be undone.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#cc3333][bold]ROUND END[/bold][/color] ───────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
An incoming [color=yellow]coronal mass ejection[/color] is announced 30 minutes before the round ends, with further warnings at 15 and 5 minutes. If your ship is still out at any of those marks, you get your own warning alongside the sector-wide one.
A ship still out when the round ends is impounded rather than lost. What that costs and how to get it back is on the [textlink="Impound Lot" link="ImpoundLot"] page.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#aa88cc][bold]SIDENOTES[/bold][/color] ───────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
- TDF, TFA and voucher crews see ACCESS DENIED on the tab. Someone else's card shows BIOMETRIC MISMATCH instead. - The Drydock Registry on the shuttle records console lists every ship by character, ship name or callsign, along with whether it is stored, underway, impounded or deregistered. - Losing a card never loses a ship. Ownership lives on the ship's own record, not on the card; a lost card only costs you the deed sitting on it.
